goals: mechanistic: quantify how increasing soil clay content shifts ELM water partitioning from deep drainage/recharge toward surface runoff, holding forcing and all other factors fixed
interpretive: characterize the shape (linear vs threshold/nonlinear) of the partitioning response across the 5-55% clay gradient
key_processes: soil hydraulic property dependence on texture (Ksat, retention/air-entry)
root-zone soil moisture storage and ET partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly partitions precipitation into surface runoff and sub-surface drainage as a function of soil hydraulic properties; clay content is set via the per-column soil lever, making a controlled synthetic sweep the natural design.

answerable: soil clay control on surface-runoff vs drainage partitioning at a single column with fixed forcing
shape/nonlinearity of partitioning response across the clay gradient (given adequate spin-up)

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — one synthetic uniform-soil column per clay treatment level
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 6 evenly spaced clay levels spanning the requested 5-55% range resolve the likely nonlinear (threshold-like) dependence of infiltration/Ksat on clay while keeping the deterministic sweep minimal; a linear-only response would be captured by fewer, but the extra levels guard against missing a threshold.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: not spatial — all treatments share one representative forcing location/period; only the soil texture (clay fraction) differs
sampling_strategy.replication: none — ELM is deterministic and forcing is identical across treatments, so replication adds no information

sampling_plan.reason: low-clay endpoint: high Ksat, expect infiltration-dominated partitioning favoring deep drainage/recharge
loamy-sand/light-loam level to trace the low-clay portion of the response curve
mid-gradient loam level to detect onset of runoff dominance
clay-loam level, likely near the infiltration-capacity transition
high-clay level: reduced Ksat, expect runoff-dominated partitioning
high-clay endpoint: minimum infiltration, maximum surface runoff, minimum recharge

validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / soil-physics literature (monotonic decline in infiltration/recharge with clay)
validation_design.comparison: analog — qualitative check that modeled partitioning shifts monotonically toward runoff with clay and that the response shape is physically plausible; no co-located observations exist for this synthetic setup
validation_design.metric: sign/monotonicity of trend and relative magnitude of runoff:recharge across treatments
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 — conceptual design, validated against expectation not data

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: synthetic uniform soil, single representative forcing location/period, clay fraction the sole varied factor, with spin-up for slow-state (recharge) equilibration

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic uniform-soil column specification with prescribed clay fraction
requires_capabilities.why: the sweep requires setting clay% directly rather than sampling SSURGO, with sand/silt co-varying by a fixed rule

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up (or WTD-informed warm start) per column
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/drainage and water table are slow states; cold-started columns read ~0 recharge and a fixed default water table, corrupting the recharge half of the partitioning

requires_capabilities.capability: partitioning diagnostics in history output (QOVER, QDRAI/QRECHARGE, ET)
requires_capabilities.why: the response variable is the runoff vs recharge split

assumptions: clay content is varied as a single-line texture gradient: as clay rises 5->55%, sand and silt co-vary by a fixed rule (user should confirm the intended sand:silt treatment)
a single representative forcing location/period within 1980-2018 is used identically for all treatments; choice of climate regime will affect absolute (not relative) partitioning
soil profile is treated as vertically uniform in texture across all layers unless the user specifies a horizoned profile
spin-up length sufficient for recharge to reach quasi-equilibrium is included (multi-year or warm start)
open_questions: How should sand vs silt co-vary as clay increases — fixed sand:silt ratio, fixed silt, or a specific textural triangle path?
Which forcing climate (wet vs dry, snow vs rain-dominated) should the controlled forcing represent — this sets whether recharge or runoff dominates the baseline?
Is a vertically uniform profile intended, or a realistic horizoned profile with the clay treatment applied to a specific layer?
Should ET be reported as a third partitioning term, or is the focus strictly the runoff:recharge split?
